study_wide_numeric_context.TG_assignment: No exact separate numerical weight loss or decomposition temperature per specimen extracted from curves.
study_wide_numeric_context.FTIR_qualification: Approximate discussion bands; Figure 4 additionally labels 3415, 1633 and 497 cm−1 on SG-V. Not all plotted labels are measured peaks of every specimen.
study_wide_numeric_context.reduction_qualification: Source-reported rounded reductions, not independently recalculated measurements.

source_interpretation.text: Sol–gel hydrolysis of zirconium n-propoxide and precipitation from zirconium oxychloride are distinct recipes. Each has oven (110 °C, 12 h) and Rotavapor vacuum (70 °C, 50 mbar, duration unreported) drying branches, followed by 400, 500, 600 or 700 °C calcination for 4 h in static air. The four uncalcined states remain separate supporting specimens.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Sections 2.1–2.3 and Scheme 1

source_interpretation.text: The paper describes purchased 70 wt% zirconium propoxide solution, dilution to 30 wt%, a 0.025 M precursor and a typical charge of 17.7 g Zr-P plus 41.3 g n-propanol. Whether the stated precursor mass denotes stock solution or neat-equivalent reagent is unresolved. No molar charge or corrected concentration is inferred.

source_interpretation.topic: Phase fractions and domain sizes are separate
source_interpretation.text: Table 1 reports XRD peak-area tetragonal/monoclinic fractions; blank cells and the printed dash do not become inferred zeros. Table 2 gives phase/reflection-specific Scherrer crystallite sizes and lattice strains, not SEM particle diameters. Its strain unit or scale is unspecified. At 700 °C, SG-O is 23 nm in Table 2 but 20 nm in the prose; both are retained with the explicit table used in structured measurements.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3,5–6, Tables 1–2 and structural discussion

source_interpretation.text: The authors relate retention of tetragonal zirconia to small crystallites, hydroxyl groups and lattice strain, with greater thermal stability for sol–gel material. Vacuum drying initially produces larger domains. These explanations and the cited critical-size literature are not additional measured thresholds or current sample recipes. Exact residual tetragonal fractions at high temperature are retained instead of treating summarized complete transformation as zero.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 4,6–7, Structural discussion and conclusions

source_interpretation.topic: Before-calcination morphology has its own scope
source_interpretation.text: Figure 6 shows spherical sol–gel particles after either drying route. Precipitation gives predominantly cubic/rectangular particles of varying sizes after oven drying, with some spherical particles after vacuum drying. These images are before calcination; no numerical SEM particle mean or automatic post-calcination shape is assigned.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 6–7, Figure 6 and Section 3.4

source_interpretation.text: Table 3 reports only before-calcination and 400 °C textural values. Surface areas and pore volumes decrease while average pore diameters increase. Figure 5 shows before-calcination N2 isotherms, interpreted as combined H2/H3 hysteresis with ink-bottle and slit pores. TG/DTG weight loss of 22–33% and mechanisms remain study-level context without exact batch-specific values.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 4–7, Thermal discussion, Figure 5, Table 3 and Sections 3.2–3.3

conflicts: Sol–gel precursor stock/dilution/0.025 M and 17.7 g +41.3 g wording is retained without resolving the charge basis.
Main p.6 prose calls Z-SG-O at700°C 20 nm; Table 2 reports23 nm. Structured values use the explicit table, with the prose discrepancy retained.
Introduction references33 and34 appear interchanged relative to bibliography topics (luminescence versus femoral heads); no external findings become current-product measurements.
SEM operating pressure is printed as >1.34×10−2 Pa; the direction is retained, not silently reversed.
Scheme 1 idealized phase arrows and prose complete transformation (96–100%) are summaries; exact Table 1 fractions, including residual tetragonal phase, take precedence in specimen fields.
limitations: Complete supplied eight-page main read, including six figures, Scheme 1, Tables 1–3 and 52 numbered references. No matching local SI located; SI and cited full sources unreviewed.
Aqueous ammonia amount, drop rate, stirring speed and exact ambient temperature are unreported. Ammonia concentration is printed as 25% without a stated mass/volume basis.

Sol–gel section states purchased 70 wt% Zr-P, dilution to 30 wt%, precursor 0.025 M and typical 17.7 g Zr-P plus 41.3 g n-propanol. The charge basis and consistency of these statements are unresolved; no molar charge or corrected concentration is calculated.

Vacuum-drying duration, rotation speed, calcination ramp/cooling and furnace/vessel geometry are unreported. Sol–gel washing is not stated; precipitation washing continues until chloride-free but volume/count are unknown.

Scherrer crystallite sizes are author-derived phase/reflection-specific domains, not SEM particle-size distributions. Lattice-strain units/scaling are not stated in Table 2. Blank cells and the printed dash remain explicit missingness rather than inferred zeros.
SEM morphology and N2 isotherms in Figures 5–6 are before calcination. Their shape is not silently transferred to calcined products. Table 3 has only before/400°C values.
Independent source comparison and molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remain pending. No measured coordinates or refined unit-cell model supplied.
